plan.title: Phone app (Android): FCM data handler that decrypts and posts notifications
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

references.label: PAN-4838 iOS sibling (shares push.ts and the fixture)

metadata.sizeJustification: One end-to-end Android feature inside apps/mobile: the FCM service, its decrypt-and-post handler, the JS registration that feeds it a token, and the tap routing that consumes its link are one user-visible behaviour (epic AC-13) and cannot be accepted separately. The file count is high because Java keeps one class per file and the Capacitor sync regenerates two Gradle files; subsystems stay at five (apps/mobile, tests/fixtures, bun.lock, .github/workflows, configuration).

narratives.Problem: The Overdeck phone app on Android cannot show notifications. The machine already seals each needs-you notification to the phone's push key (PAN-4843) and the directory already forwards it to FCM as a data-only message {s: <sealed>} (PAN-4830), but the app has no FirebaseMessagingService, no FCM token registration, no notification permission request and no tap routing, so nothing reaches the operator when the app is closed.
narratives.Proposal: Add a Java OverdeckMessagingService that is the only MESSAGING_EVENT service (the @capacitor/push-notifications service is removed with tools:node="remove"), opens the sealed payload with lazysodium and the Keystore-wrapped push key from SecureStore, and posts it on the needs-you or updates channel with a tap link ai.overdeck.app:/open#v=1&e=&p=&t=. Keep @capacitor/push-notifications for the permission and token; a small OverdeckPush plugin reports whether Firebase is configured so JS never calls a crashing register(). JS sends push-register on each online transition, routes the open link to the paired machine, and Settings shows the notification state. Decrypt, parse and posting are covered by JVM (JUnit + Robolectric) tests that CI runs; google-services.json and the emulator AC-13 run follow once PAN-4841 creates the Firebase project.
narratives.NonGoals:
- iOS push, the Notification Service Extension and apsEnvironment (PAN-4838)
- The iOS Live Activity (PAN-4839)
- Creating the Firebase project, FCM service account, directory secrets, upload keystore or store listings (PAN-4841)
- Calling PUT /api/phones/self/push-key from Android; the push key never rotates
- An in-app notifications on/off switch; the Android system setting is the switch
- Suppressing the system notification while the app is in the foreground, or an in-app toast
- Notification action buttons, grouping or summary notifications, per-machine channels, custom sounds
- Fixing Android Force stop blocking FCM (documented only)
- Direct-boot delivery before first unlock
- Any change to services/connect, src/lib/push, or packages/contracts
- Adding Kotlin to the Android project
- Logging notification titles, bodies, tokens or keys anywhere

autoDecisions.summary: Write the Android code in Java (OverdeckMessagingService.java), not Kotlin as the epic names it.
autoDecisions.rationale: All existing Android app code is Java and the project has no Kotlin Gradle plugin; adding a toolchain for one class is scope creep with CI risk.

autoDecisions.summary: Keep @capacitor/push-notifications for permission and token, remove its MessagingService from the merged manifest, and forward onNewToken to PushNotificationsPlugin.onNewToken.
autoDecisions.rationale: Two services bound to MESSAGING_EVENT resolve arbitrarily and only ours posts when the app is closed; the plugin is still the shared JS API PAN-4838 uses on iOS.

autoDecisions.summary: Post a placeholder ('Overdeck' / 'Something needs you') when a push cannot be opened; post nothing when the push keys are absent (signed out).
autoDecisions.rationale: Matches the iOS placeholder behaviour in the epic (D-5) and avoids high-priority FCM messages with no visible result; a signed-out phone has no reason to show anything.

autoDecisions.summary: Add an OverdeckPush Android plugin whose status() reports whether a FirebaseApp exists, and call register() only when it does.
autoDecisions.rationale: PushNotificationsPlugin.register() calls FirebaseMessaging.getInstance() and crashes the app when google-services.json is absent, which is the state until PAN-4841 finishes.

autoDecisions.summary: Resend push-register on every transition of the directory socket to online instead of tracking a last-sent token.
autoDecisions.rationale: The directory update is idempotent and resending heals a registration it cleared after a dead token; no extra state to persist.

autoDecisions.summary: Settings shows notification state with a Turn on button when Android can still prompt, and no in-app switch.
autoDecisions.rationale: Epic hazard H-4 asks Settings to show how to turn notifications on; the system setting is the authoritative switch.

autoDecisions.summary: Own the shared fixture tests/fixtures/phone-push/ here and keep src/native/push.ts platform-neutral with an iOS stub branch.
autoDecisions.rationale: PAN-4838 names the same paths and is planned concurrently; whichever lands second extends rather than re-creates.

autoDecisions.summary: Gate the final device-acceptance item on PAN-4841 (healthz fcm:true and a committed google-services.json) and signal the flywheel if it is missing, instead of pulling operator console actions into this plan.
autoDecisions.rationale: Creating a Firebase project needs the operator's Google account; the issue body says google-services.json comes from that setup (W-REL1).

autoDecisions.summary: Test real crypto with lazysodium-java in plain JUnit and posting under Robolectric, with an androidTest fallback (CP-1).
autoDecisions.rationale: lazysodium-android ships only Android ABI natives, so a JVM test needs the desktop twin; Robolectric's ShadowNotificationManager makes posting checkable in CI without an emulator.

Wire it in ShellApp with a pushEpoch-keyed effect after the services effect. Add unregisterPush to SignOutDeps as step `push token` before push-unregister.
